variants.title: Plain Explorer
variants.prompt:
[image_picker_background_preview]
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: comparable desktop GUI style exploration, illustrative future interface, not an actual screenshot or a precise security diagram.
Primary request: one complete kisib.dub-sar Windows 11 certificate explorer window with a genuinely classic Windows 95 Explorer visual style: square corners, native grey beveled controls, navy title bar, white list/tree areas, compact Tahoma or MS Sans Serif typography, dotted tree connectors and tiny plus/minus branch boxes. Flat front-on view, landscape 1536 x 1024 composition, crisp and readable. The application fills the picture. No surrounding computer, wallpaper, device frame, modern dashboard, rounded cards, glass effects, gradients, giant icons, neon, backup controls, import controls, delete controls, or implementation claims.
Fixed content across all three directions: title bar "kisib.dub-sar"; File, Certificate, View, Help menus; toolbar buttons "Refresh", "History log", "Countries"; tree permanently visible on the left about 30% width; list/grid on the right; Details and "Issuer 🏛️" tabs beneath the list. Above the tree, native small dropdowns "Group: Country" and "Sort: Name".
Tree must show TWO parallel branches: "Windows stores", with LOCAL_MACHINE > Root > .Default and CURRENT_USER; and "Grouped views", whose virtual organizational groups do not change real Windows paths. In Grouped views show country rows "RU Russia 🌿🧱🇷🇺", "UA Ukraine", "GB United Kingdom 👑", plus separate tag branches "👑 Monarchy", "🌿 Custom", "🧱 BRICS", "🇷🇺 Russia". Under EACH of these four tag branches show indented sibling folders "Enabled" and "Blocked". Show additional collapsed custom groups "🏛️", "💀", "💃". Russia belongs to THREE independent tag groups 🌿, 🧱, 🇷🇺. Do not collapse them into one category. One certificate may appear in several virtual groups. All monarchy country grouping labels carry 👑.
Right-side data must be explicitly fictional sample certificates "Example Root A", "Example Root B", "Example Root C"; no real CA trust verdicts. Sample country/tag rows RU / 🌿🧱🇷🇺; GB / 👑; AE / 👑🌿🧱. Enabled and Blocked are proposed user policy states. Show a compact label "Policy preview · Enforcement to test". Software scope/observed usage must say "Not evaluated". Never claim a certificate is currently being used merely because it exists in a store.
Details include full Subject/Issuer labels, "Key: RSA 2048", "Signature: SHA-256", "SPKI SHA-256", a concise visible row of custom country/tag labels, and a distinct "History log" button with scope dropdown "Certificate / Issuer / Group / Software". Source country and CA owner country have separate labels; missing data says "Unknown".
A small bracket area represents the future chain view: fictional leaf/issuer/root certificate panels joined in a simple playoff-inspired shape ending at a "Software scope" panel labeled "Not evaluated". Make it a UI style sketch, not an asserted observed topology. Include the compact label "Chain view [to test]". Do not use hashes as parent links. Small inline text "[documented]" for certificate Subject/Issuer; "[to test]" on grouping/enforcement/chain/usage.
Keep readable text, restrained tiny emoji labels, a proper Explorer tree with clearly visible connectors, and a status bar "Design preview · Sample data · Read-only v0.1". Rendering style is the only variable; do not alter the functional scope.
Visual direction: Plain Explorer. Closest to a clean Windows 95 file manager / MMC. Compact 3D bevels, thin toolbar, modest tree rows, dense text. The upper right contains a traditional sortable certificate list with Subject, Country, Tags, Policy, Scope columns. The lower right contains native Details / Issuer 🏛️ / Chain tabs. Show a small playoff bracket within the lower pane alongside plain certificate details, without oversized cards. The whole design is utilitarian, legible, orderly. A selected navy row and small text state indicators provide hierarchy.
CRITICAL LATEST USER CORRECTION: issuer organizing controls belong in the FAR LEFT Explorer sidebar. At the very top of the left sidebar put the label "Issuer explorer 🏛️", then a native "Find issuer" search box and compact "Group by" and "Sort by" dropdowns. The default grouping is Country, default sorting Name. The left tree owns issuer selection, search, grouping, and sorting; the right area shows results, playoff grid, and details. Put issuer country/tag branches ABOVE the Windows stores branch. All previous functional and old Windows style requirements remain. Show clear plus/minus boxes and dotted branch lines. No separate modern organizing sidebar or control dashboard on the right.
